proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof ((a) smoothness, (b) support, (c) derivative of the convolution, (d) uniform convergence), for one mollification radius. The parent uses r_ℓ = δ/(ℓ+1) and takes ℓ with r_ℓ ≤ r₀. Here we take directly r := min r₀ δ for the given ε, which is exactly what step 3(d) needs. The mollifier of step 2 is the sibling lemma dgcr_stc_exists_normalized_mollifier.
Notation: ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure volume; ∂ᵥf(x) := Df(x)v = fderiv ℝ f x v; convolution (ρ ⋆ f)(x) := ∫ ρ(t)·f(x − t) dt, i.e. Mathlib's convolution ρ f (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume.
1. Uniform continuity of ∂ᵥφ. φ is C¹, so Dφ = fderiv ℝ φ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv with 1 ≠ 0). Dφ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). Let g(x) := ∂ᵥφ(x) = fderiv ℝ φ x v. Then g is continuous (Continuous.clm_apply with the constant function v). It has compact support by HasCompactSupport.comp_left, since evaluation at v, L ↦ L v, sends 0 to 0. A continuous function with compact support is uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). By Metric.uniformContinuous_iff there is r₀ > 0 with dist (g a) (g b) < ε whenever dist a b < r₀.
2. Mollifier. Put r := min r₀ δ; then r > 0 (lt_min, since r₀ > 0 and δ > 0), r ≤ r₀ and r ≤ δ. The sibling lemma dgcr_stc_exists_normalized_mollifier, applied to n and r, gives ρ : Euclid n → ℝ with: ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ρ, HasCompactSupport ρ, ρ ≥ 0 pointwise, ∫ ρ = 1, and support ρ ⊆ ball 0 r. ρ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous), hence locally integrable (Continuous.locallyIntegrable).
3. Define ψ := ρ ⋆ φ = convolution ρ φ (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume.
4. Smoothness. ψ is C^∞ (order (⊤ : ℕ∞)) by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with L = lsmul ℝ ℝ. Its hypotheses: the left factor ρ is compactly supported and ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞); the right factor φ is locally integrable, being continuous (C¹; Continuous.locallyIntegrable).
5. Support. By support_convolution_subset, support ψ ⊆ support ρ + support φ. Let z ∈ support ψ and write z = a + b with a ∈ support ρ and b ∈ support φ (Set.mem_add). Then ‖a‖ < r since support ρ ⊆ ball 0 r, and b ∈ tsupport φ (subset_tsupport). Hence dist z b = ‖(a + b) − b‖ = ‖a‖ < r ≤ δ. So z ∈ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) (mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Thus support ψ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ). The closed thickening is closed (isClosed_cthickening), so tsupport ψ = closure (support ψ) ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) (closure_minimal).
6. Compact support. tsupport φ is compact (HasCompactSupport φ), so cthickening δ (tsupport φ) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; Euclid n is a proper space). tsupport ψ is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and contained in it by step 5. Hence tsupport ψ is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), i.e. HasCompactSupport ψ.
7. Derivative of ψ. Fix x. HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right applies with L = lsmul ℝ ℝ: ρ is locally integrable, and φ is compactly supported and ContDiff ℝ 1. It says ψ has Fréchet derivative convolution ρ (fderiv ℝ φ) (ContinuousLinearMap.precompR (Euclid n) (lsmul ℝ ℝ)) volume x at x. Hence fderiv ℝ ψ x equals this (HasFDerivAt.fderiv). Evaluate at v with convolution_precompR_apply, using that ρ is locally integrable and Dφ is compactly supported and continuous (step 1). This gives fderiv ℝ ψ x v = convolution ρ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x = (ρ ⋆ g)(x).
8. Estimate. Keep x fixed. For every y ∈ ball x r, dist y x < r ≤ r₀, so dist (g y) (g x) < ε by step 1. Apply dist_convolution_le with these inputs: 0 ≤ ε; R := r with support ρ ⊆ ball 0 r; ρ ≥ 0 pointwise and ∫ ρ = 1; g AE-strongly measurable (it is continuous: Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable); z₀ := g(x); and dist (g y) z₀ ≤ ε for all y ∈ ball x r. It yields dist ((ρ ⋆ g)(x)) (g(x)) ≤ ε. By step 7 and Real.dist_eq, this is |fderiv ℝ ψ x v − fderiv ℝ φ x v| ≤ ε.
9. ψ has the four required properties: smooth (step 4), compactly supported (step 6), tsupport ψ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) (step 5), and the derivative bound for every x (step 8). ∎
key_steps: ∂ᵥφ is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous: pick r₀ > 0 with |∂ᵥφ(a) − ∂ᵥφ(b)| < ε when dist a b < r₀.
